key_insight: The paper turns the nonlocal Grad--Mercier rank law into a clipped, mass-lumped discrete formulation that yields a strictly convex finite element energy and a unique equilibrium.
engineering_relevance: This provides a robust FEM pathway for magnetic equilibrium problems with plateaued solutions, enabling reliable computation on practical polygonal domains.
method: Use conforming piecewise affine finite elements on polygonal meshes.
Replace the continuum rank law with an equivalent clipped nonnegative law and a mass-lumped nodal measure.
Assign tied nodal values a common rank interval to preserve lumped mass and ensure strict convexity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports meshwise convergence of the discrete equilibria in $H^1_0(\Omega)$ and uniformly on $\overline\Omega$, plus weak-* convergence of reconstructed sources in $L^\infty(\Omega)$ to the continuum source.
watch_item: The convergence and boundedness guarantees rely on meshes satisfying a discrete comparison principle, so implementation quality and mesh structure matter.
paper_title: A Finite Element Method for the Grad--Mercier Equation
